At Least 40 Dead and Millions Without Power After Hurricane Helene Made Landfall: What We Know So Far
Helene was a Category 4 hurricane when it made landfall, but has since been downgraded
At least 40 people have been killed across multiple states and millions of people are without power after Hurricane Helene made landfall over Florida's Big Bend on Thursday, Sept. 26.
The latest death toll, which has risen since Helene hit Florida, was reported by the Associated Press and The New York Times.
The majority of the victims were in Georgia and South Carolina, according to the Times.
Helene was a Category 4 storm when it made landfall around 11:10 p.m. local time near Perry, Fla., and has since been steadily downgraded, now to a post-tropical cyclone, according to the National Hurricane Center.
In just a matter of hours, Helene delivered damaging wind gusts as well as "catastrophic, life-threatening, [and] record-breaking" flooding in many areas, especially the higher terrains of the southeastern Appalachians, where "numerous significant landslides" are also expected through Friday, Sept. 27.
As of Friday evening more than 3 million people were without power in Florida, Georgia, the Carolinas, Virginia and beyond, according to PowerOutage.us.
The death include 11 in Georgia, Gov. Brian Kemp said during a news conference on Friday morning.
Two of the victims died in Jeff Davis County when a trailer was picked up by strong winds and thrown into a nearby peanut field, according to ABC affiliate WJCL.
In Blackshear, officials said part-time assistant fire chief Vernon "Leon" Davis died after a tree fell on his vehicle Friday morning, according to First Coast News.
Deaths were also reported in Laurel, Liberty and Laurens counties, WJCL reported.

Meanwhile, there have been seven confirmed deaths in Florida, according to the Times.
One person died after a sign fell on top of a car traveling on Interstate 4 in Tampa, and another person died in Dixie County after a tree fell onto their home, CBS affiliate WINK reported. Five people also died in Pinnellas County, Sheriff Bob Gualtieri announced during a news conference on Friday, per the Times.
A person also died in Charlotte, North Carolina, after a tree fell onto another home around 5 a.m., according to CBS affiliate WBTV. Two people were killed by falling trees in South Carolina on Friday, as well, per NBC affiliate WYFF.
Sustained winds from Tropical Storm Helene had slowed to just 40 mph by Friday, and storm surge is expected to subside by the end of Friday, according to the NHC.
President Joe Biden declared a state of emergency for Florida on Tuesday, Sept. 24, and ordered "Federal assistance to supplement State, tribal, and local response efforts due to the emergency conditions resulting from Tropical Storm Helene beginning on September 23, 2024, and continuing."
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis announced in a post on X that Florida had almost 18,000 linemen staged along with available search and rescue and roadway clearing crews.
